title: Cop fired to save partner, court told: Officer shot man wielding knives 10 times in back: [FINAL C Edition]
article: A rookie Vancouver police officer with just six weeks on the job says he shot several times at a knife-wielding attacker slashing at his partner in a dark, Downtown Eastside lane because he wasn't sure the bullets were hitting the man.
In chilling testimony at a coroner's inquest detailing the seconds leading up to the death of Gerald Chenery on Boxing Day night 2004,
Const. Bryan Smith said he feared he was shooting his own partner.

"\[The shooting\] didn't appear to have an effect on him," said the beefy officer, who fired 10 bullets into Chenery's back and one into his front as he tackled Const. Elizabeth Clark into a fence, landing on top of her before turning to Smith.
"I honestly thought I was missing him," Smith said. "I was concerned that some of my rounds had hit her."
Clark loudly sobbed as her partner described what was going through his mind.
"I could hear her underneath him," he said. "While she was there, I could hear her screaming, fight-for-life screaming. I thought, 'I need to stop him now or she's going to die.'"
The inquest heard how two rookies -- Clark, 37, had just eight weeks on the job -- were working together over Christmas because of limited available senior staff.

On routine patrol, they discovered Chenery had a warrant for his arrest and was a violent ex-federal inmate. Smith, who got out to handcuff Chenery, ended up pulling his firearm on Chenery after the man told Smith he had a weapon.
The 125-pound Clark said she initially pulled out her baton -- "Big guy, little me, baton" -- before she realized the 200-pound Chenery was armed.
"She saw I had a gun and she ducked in behind me," testified Smith, who called out to Clark to radio for backup as he yelled at Chenery to drop what he could then see was a knife.
"Don't make me shoot you," he said he told the man.
But Chenery, now with a knife in each hand, ran toward Clark, who was now armed and standing alone. She fired four shots; three missed Chenery and one hit him in the groin.
Smith said: "When \[Chenery\] was moving toward her was when I began \[shooting\]."
She said that while trapped under Chenery, she was "striking his head with my firearm because I've got nothing left" and that she was able to crawl away on hands and knees as backup officers arrived.
"Then I realize, 'Holy crap, I've dropped my gun," which she quickly retrieved.
